reviews.text: I rely on this doctor as my primary care physician. It can be crowded and the wait times can be long, but I trust them and continue to go there.
The staff and veterinarians are all kind, and I feel completely at ease leaving my pet in their care.

This clinic is very clean, and the kind and attentive service from the doctors and staff gives me a great sense of security. Last year, when my beloved Hanako passed away at the age of 13, I was able to cope with the loss thanks to Dr. Takei, her primary veterinarian. Even now, I feel confident bringing my 15-year-old dog to this clinic for treatment.

Thank you so much.
The explanations were thorough and easy to understand; I think it's a really good hospital.

In May, my cockatiel suffered from metal poisoning, and since I couldn't get an appointment at my regular vet, I was searching for a nearby clinic when I saw a review here mentioning that they treat birds. I contacted them out of desperation.

It was a great hospital, so I'm posting this review now in case it's helpful to other bird owners.

My bird was in a very critical condition, vomiting and losing weight, but they managed it with daytime hospitalization. (They don't seem to offer nighttime hospitalization.)
They even called me when my bird vomited severely.

At home, they prescribed oral chelating agents and vitamins, as well as yeast to aid digestion.

There's only one veterinarian who specializes in birds, so on their days off, you basically have to manage the bird at home.

(When my bird became critically ill on a day the veterinarian was off, they referred me to another exotic bird specialist hospital where the veterinarian has furthered their expertise.)

Thanks to their diligent treatment, my bird is now very healthy.

Points of concern:
- Waiting time
→ When my bird was in a critical condition, they prioritized it and it was quick, but when the treatment was nearing its end, even with online registration, I waited about 2.5 hours.
- Waiting area is shared with dogs and cats
→ This might be scary for timid birds.
- Strong smell of pet deodorizer
→ You can wait outside, but the waiting room has a strong smell of pet deodorizer.

I would like to use your services again if needed.
Thank you.
It's great in every way, except it's a bit far from the station.

My pet lovebird injured its leg, so I took it to the vet. It was my first time going to a veterinary clinic, so I called first, and the receptionist was very kind and helpful (telling me about the availability of a vet who treats birds, the clinic's busy schedule, etc.).
Afternoon appointments were taken from 3 PM, and consultations started at 4 PM. I arrived at 3 PM, got a numbered ticket, and waited in the waiting room. The clinic was very clean and comfortable.
At 4 PM, I was seen immediately and told that it was just a bruise and that I should keep my bird as still as possible. A stool test was also performed, and I was told my bird was healthy.
The vet explained everything very clearly and kindly, including the benefits and drawbacks of X-rays and medication, and general health management. The vet also owns a lovebird, which made me feel at ease during the consultation.
Although the injury was partly due to my carelessness, the vet didn't blame me at all and instead offered encouragement.
It's rare to find a vet who treats birds, so I'm fortunate to have this clinic near my home; it's a great relief. It's best if you don't need to go to the hospital at all, but if something does happen, I would like to use your services again.

My dog ​​had a terrible skin rash, but they suggested various treatment methods. Thanks to changing his food, and diligently using shampoos and moisturizers every day, the bright red bumps have now disappeared, and his skin is beautifully white. I'm truly grateful for their help every time!

My cat's life was saved!
A urinary tract stone was discovered during a health checkup at our regular vet. Because it was a difficult surgery, only a limited number of hospitals could perform it, and we were advised to seek a second opinion as soon as possible, with recommendations for university hospitals and other options. However, I had some reservations and searched for this hospital online. A week later, I visited for an initial consultation. It wasn't possible to reschedule the surgery, and the head veterinarian was available that day or tomorrow, so they performed emergency surgery. It was truly fortunate timing, and thanks to the highly experienced doctors and equipment, I feel like my cat was saved by a hair's breadth. The surgery was successful, and she was able to be discharged. She still needs care, but I truly believe she wouldn't have survived without this hospital, and I am incredibly grateful.
The staff were also very kind and helpful, even when busy, making it a trustworthy hospital.

Postscript
It's been about a year since the surgery.
She's doing very well! Because not everyone is guaranteed to recover, I cherish the life that was saved, hoping every day that there will be no recurrence! Thank you.

I've been a patient here since before the hospital moved.

The head doctor and all the other doctors are kind and dedicated to providing excellent treatment. You can reserve an appointment online and choose your preferred doctor through a questionnaire.

Even with an appointment, there's quite a long wait, but that's understandable considering there are emergency cases and seriously ill children, and I think it's a hospital worth the wait. They have the latest medical equipment, highly motivated doctors and staff, and provide top-notch medical care comparable to a university hospital.

On the other hand, recently it's become a little more difficult to go for minor symptoms or just a quick consultation. (Although the doctors always say to call anytime.) I miss the days when the head doctor always saw me, but being able to hear the opinions of various doctors is also a benefit.

*Please see below for parking information!!*

I used this clinic for a second opinion on my friend's dog.

The diagnosis was completely different from that of a certain general animal hospital. It was a real lifesaver!!

We stopped all medication and switched the food. Actually, the food recommended by the other hospital was the exact opposite.

This doctor said, "Please call anytime if anything unusual happens, and we'll take responsibility and see your dog even in the middle of the night."

After hearing that, it's no longer just a second-opinion hospital, is it? This has become our main hospital.

*Parking Notice*↓↓↓
Parking is limited to 4 cars. There are 2 spaces behind the entrance, and 2 more spaces, for a total of 4 spaces.

If the two cars in the back need to leave first, you need to ask a staff member to move the car in front.

There are coin-operated parking lots nearby, but...it's a residential area with one-way streets, so parking can be a gamble...

It had been a while since I'd had an urgent need, so I went without an appointment right when they opened, but there was a line of people all the way to the elevator entrance. I don't know if it was because appointments weren't available or what, but I didn't think I'd be able to get seen in the morning, so I went to the relatively nearby K*** Animal Hospital.

There probably aren't any good animal hospitals around here.

I used to think it was expensive, but other hospitals have raised their prices, so I actually thought it was cheap now.

Later, when I went before they opened in the afternoon, I was seen right away.

I think I'll take all my animals there from now on.

I'm always grateful for Dr. Ino's care. This time, he performed surgery for kidney stones on me. He's a wonderful doctor—kind, helpful, and reliable!

While the waiting time is longer and the prices are a little higher than other clinics, it's such a great clinic that it doesn't matter at all—the other doctors and staff are all so kind!
The veterinarians were incredibly kind and attentive, which was wonderful. I think it's by far the best animal hospital I've ever been to. I was also surprised by how reasonable the prices were.
It's clean. Reservations can be made 30 minutes before your appointment. It tends to get crowded in the morning even before your appointment.

Dr. Ino was in charge of our care. Thank you so much for taking such good care of us despite your busy schedule.

This is a very good hospital with highly skilled doctors and well-equipped facilities for laparoscopic surgery. They even provide blood transfusions on the same day if necessary. I wholeheartedly recommend it.

The doctors were young, enthusiastic, and provided attentive care. My child is usually very afraid of hospitals, but he went into this hospital without any hesitation each time. It seems the staff took very good care of him.

This is the hospital that saved the lives of two out of my three pets.

You need to be prepared for a wait. I make online reservations and go home after checking in. I can't wait forever. But I can't change hospitals. I'm grateful that they're open on weekends and holidays.

My dog's regular vet was on holiday for the New Year period, and he had a seizure due to his chronic epilepsy, so I took him to the vet as a precaution.

Because of the holiday period, I was 32nd in line, and at first I wondered how long the wait would be. However, I received a call sooner than I expected, and the vet, Dr. Hashimoto, was very thorough. He explained that he couldn't decide whether an emergency injection was necessary without checking the amount of medication my dog ​​was currently taking. In the end, he determined that my dog ​​was calm and didn't need an injection.

Although it's a busy hospital, they have five examination rooms, and the consultations were conducted smoothly. I think it's a very good hospital.
The examination was thorough. I felt at ease after being examined there.
If it's not too crowded, this is the best veterinarian.

[Addendum]
Since the start of fiscal year 2025, with the exception of one receptionist, the question "Can I use insurance?" has not been asked at the time of payment.
Pre-operative tests should have been covered by insurance, but they weren't, resulting in a high cost, and subsequent applications were rejected.
As of September 2025, only the always pleasant person at reception asks this question.
It's inconvenient that it varies depending on the person, so I would like it to be standardized.

I've been going there for about six months. I have two kittens, and one had its neutering surgery completed here.
Since they are still kittens and haven't had any major problems, I haven't requested a specific veterinarian, so the younger doctors whose names I won't mention here, but both of them make eye contact with the cats and talk to them properly.
I'll refrain from mentioning names in this day and age, but they are a bright and straightforward woman and a kind and gentle man.
Even though I went for a minor issue, they thoroughly examined my cat while talking to me and prescribed regular medication.
They also clearly explained the price of the medication.

I was surprised that the nurse or receptionist kept casually talking about other patients while I was speaking.
Regarding that, I think it's common sense to excuse yourself before discussing your business, especially during an examination. The conversation wasn't urgent (I could hear everything), and it didn't feel very good.
This is the only reason I deducted a star.

Incidentally, it might depend on the personality of the animal, but for vaccinations, a nurse doesn't accompany them. I've never had one. This is something I can handle myself, and nowadays, some people are quite particular about how they handle their pets, so it's not a problem.

I've never waited 2-3 hours. This might be because I choose to go on days with bad weather since my pet isn't sick...
The parking lot is a little inconvenient to enter and exit, but if you don't like it, you can use one of the many coin-operated parking lots nearby, so it's not a problem.

The neutering surgery was performed by the aforementioned male doctor. He explained everything with photos taken during the surgery.

I thought the anesthesia wore off a little slowly, but after the surgery, there was no discomfort or swelling, and it's in a really nice state. (At another clinic where a sibling of mine was taken, the recovery from anesthesia was quick, but the post-operative swelling was severe.)
Many people talk about the skill of a veterinarian in administering anesthesia, but ultimately, it comes down to whether the clinic is a good fit for you and your family (pet).
Since it's a human interaction, if it's not a good fit, you can always go to another clinic.
Considering all of that, I've chosen to go to this clinic because the doctors are thorough and reliable, the clinic is clean, and there's absolutely no odor.

The words the male doctor said to me during my first visit here—"Please touch your pet in many different places on a regular basis so that they don't have any unpleasant experiences"—really struck me and were very important.
I still struggle a bit with trimming the nails on the hind legs, but thanks to regularly touching the inside of their mouth, they hardly mind having their teeth brushed anymore.
Thank you.
This will continue to be the first hospital I go to.

I had my husky groomed.
They did a great job, and they kept him until 6pm, so I was able to pick him up in the evening when the heat had subsided.

The two groomers who assisted me worked in perfect unison, and they were so adorable, like the twins from the horror movie The Shining.

I'd love to use their services again.

I've been receiving their care for about three years.
There are not many hospitals that treat sugar gliders and rabbits, so I found them by chance. The doctor is very kind and will consult with you to decide on the direction of treatment.

My parents' dog is also treated here, and I highly recommend them as they are always available to help with any issues.

This wasn't my dog's regular vet, but I came after reading reviews because my dog's condition suddenly worsened.
The doctor in charge was incredibly thorough in explaining everything and dedicated himself to thoroughly investigating the cause and providing treatment until the very end. Sadly, due to my dog's age and pre-existing conditions, he passed away.
However, if my next dog ever needs treatment, I plan to bring him back here.
I knew there would be a long wait, but even when I was the only one there to pay, I still had to wait a long time... My dog's strength was running out... I was so worried, constantly thinking about the time he had left.
Thanks to the dedicated treatment of the doctors and staff, my dog ​​fought hard for just a few days... and I was truly relieved that I could be with him in my arms until the end.
I think that's what he wanted too.
Thank you so much.

I take my cat to this vet. The wait times are long and the fees are high, but recently my beloved cat wasn't getting better, and although I considered other hospitals, my trust in this one ultimately prevailed, and I continue to go there.

Exactly one year ago, I took my cat to this hospital when she caught a cold. A young male veterinarian was very kind and gave her a thorough examination.

At that time, he recommended a PCR test based on her symptoms, but it would cost several tens of thousands of yen, which was a bit too expensive for us, so we decided against the test and instead he prescribed eye drops and nasal drops.

However, her symptoms didn't improve at all until we finished the medication, so I became worried and took her to another animal hospital. At that hospital, I was told that "the viruses that cause feline colds are very limited, and a general cat cold medicine is sufficient," and after trying that medicine, she recovered immediately.

While the veterinarian's care was thorough, ultimately, the examination and treatment at the other hospital proved successful.

I've been using this service since my dog's spay/neuter surgery, and I also always have him groomed and stay at the hotel. 
The doctors and staff are very kind, and their skills are trustworthy, so I can leave him in their care with peace of mind. My dog ​​always seems happy, and it seems he remembers the doctors and staff. I feel that it's inevitable that a good place can be busy, so I'm grateful that they've put in a lot of effort and trial and error with the various apps and automation they use. I'm very lucky that it's less than a 10-minute drive from my house. I look forward to continuing to use their services.

I've been using this hospital for checkups, tests, surgeries, and grooming since it opened.
The experienced reception staff are efficient, and the doctors are knowledgeable, kind, and provide excellent service.
However, I think the number of patients has increased considerably since the beginning, so the waiting times seem to have increased as well. But I think it's unavoidable when it comes to my beloved dog.
I just have to brace myself when it's time for heartworm checkups and general health checks.

I downloaded the online reception and an app called Melp, and filled out a medical questionnaire while I waited.

Have the unusually long wait times been improved somewhat? They seem to be working hard, trying new things.

It seems like a young, very friendly person has joined the reception desk. While I was killing time, I spoke to the pet owner next to me, and he said that the rude receptionist is still there, but that she's a new receptionist.

I guess everyone feels the same way.

We all got excited about how nice the new receptionist is, but...

When you work there long enough, everyone gets used to the service, and as you become more senior, no one questions your customer service attitude. I hope the new receptionist keeps her cute smile.

The facilities, doctors, and nurses are great. The wait time averages 2-3 hours, so you still have to wait. Even if you make an online reservation, you still have to wait. The reason I gave it a 1 star is because of the receptionist. They're rude, never smile, and have no sense of customer service.

They've been talking about customer harassment lately, but I'm not asking for too much. It would be a great veterinary hospital if they treated each pet with a smile and compassionate care.
Veterinary hospitals are places where beloved, precious creatures, like family members, go because they are worried about some kind of problem, so when they are treated with an unnecessarily suspicious attitude or a sharp, glaring gaze and a cold attitude, it makes you feel so frustrated you could cry.
People who use this hospital will immediately know who the receptionist is.
When watching the explanations given to new patients, they are so unfriendly and have dead eyes that you feel sorry for them, and you can tell they are treating them with irritation, making you wonder, ``Are they glaring at me?''
Please, please treat them with a smile, even if it's just a polite smile. I would appreciate a more considerate attitude toward customers, and consideration for their feelings.

As I wrote at the beginning, I think the doctors, nurses, and facilities are all top-notch. That's why I think they have so many patients, even with such a terrible receptionist.

I hope this opinion is heard and shared within the hospital.

Two years ago, I had seven kidney stones, and I was able to pass six of them with supplements. The remaining one was fractured with a laser. Other hospitals immediately told me I needed open surgery, so I'm really glad I went to this hospital. I want to continue receiving care at this hospital for a long time to come.

I took my lovebird to a bird hospital in Ikebukuro, but it didn't get any better, so I went to this hospital for a second opinion.
The diagnosis was very accurate, and they suggested various tests which I understood well. The consultation fee was also reasonable compared to the Ikebukuro hospital. I regret not going to this hospital from the beginning; the difference was that significant.
It's been a week since the examination, and the oral medication they prescribed has made a big difference in its condition.
I'm getting another bird, so I plan to have a health checkup there once things settle down.

The bird hospital in Ikebukuro is famous, but the consultation fees are high, and you can't expect accurate treatment. I will never go there again.

My beloved dog's life has been extended by four years. Despite having cancer, he was in excellent health for almost four years. At the age of six, he was diagnosed with a serious illness (inflammatory bowel disease), and we repeatedly transferred him to animal hospitals in Kita Ward, Itabashi Ward, and Toshima Ward. By the time he was eight, even the treatment by the head veterinarian at a large, popular animal hospital where we had been taking care of him for a year had reached its limits, and he was in a very dangerous condition. There were no remaining treatment options, his blood test results were poor, and detailed examinations requiring anesthesia were no longer possible. We were able to reduce his medication, which had been difficult at other hospitals, and the doctor was quite good, but seeing the end of my dog's life was unbearable for me. I doted on him and raised him with such care. I couldn't let him die so easily. In the midst of all this, I finally found this hospital, and after examinations, cancer was found. It was an incurable cancer, and I was despairing, but he lived for four years, without being bedridden or needing care, without diapers, and he was able to walk until the very end. My body was worn out after four years of chemotherapy and six years of steroids, but my child was healthy, and the third year was the most stable. If we hadn't found this hospital, my child would undoubtedly have passed away without an endoscopy, without the hidden cancer being discovered. Sadly, my child was also taking immunosuppressants (medications that suppress the body's ability to destroy cancer cells) as part of treatment for a rare disease, which was the exact opposite of what was needed. After transferring to this hospital, the chemotherapy that was started immediately had a great effect, and my child recovered remarkably quickly. Since surgery was not an option for this type of cancer, and chemotherapy and steroids were the only treatment options, we started high-dose vitamin C intravenous therapy simultaneously with chemotherapy to broaden the treatment options. I requested this treatment myself, and my child loved it and continued it for four years. It was completely different from what I had expected, and I felt a definite improvement; it was a very satisfying treatment. This infusion gives a great boost of energy, and my child became stronger. I am etched in my memory the surprising actions and changes of my child, and the sight of him walking briskly through the harsh winter cold, cutting through the wind. I will never forget it. The other day, I met a child who has been receiving this IV drip for six months, and he is feeling much better and doing well. I think that each child will show their own unique, much more energetic self than usual. My husband calls this IV drip "doping (lol)." I don't understand why something like this makes them feel better; it's a mystery. It was a pretty good treatment! I recommend it. My child had ozone therapy five times, but in his case, it had absolutely no effect. Maybe it depends on the individual. I apologize for only writing reviews about cancer treatment. Lastly, Oji Pet Clinic has special and excellent reviews such as "a life was saved," "the disease was discovered," "a miracle," and "they were able to perform treatments, tests, and surgeries that were difficult at other clinics," and patients come from all over the country. My other child is currently receiving treatment there. This is a highly recommended hospital.

We love all furry animals – dogs, cats, rabbits, ferrets, hamsters, and more! We hope all your adorable pets stay healthy!

Thank you for the care you provided for my beloved cat. The examination was very thorough, and thanks to Dr. Ino's kind and caring treatment in particular, my cat is doing well and I am very grateful. I would like to have Dr. Ino examine my cat again if I need anything. Thank you very much.

My dog ​​is about to undergo surgery, but the doctor and staff are always smiling and the atmosphere is very pleasant, which puts me at ease. It seems like there are many regular patients, and everyone is smiling and chatting happily. I think this shows the high quality of the clinic. The doctor's explanations are detailed, polite, and easy to understand, and if I have any questions, they take the time to answer them thoroughly. It's far from my home, but I'm glad I chose this clinic!

I took my dog ​​there the other day, but after waiting for over three hours, they refused to make a reservation for him and didn't even examine him. They may have been busy, but they didn't give me any explanation and just wasted my time. The attitude of all the staff was very rude and unfriendly. Also, while I was waiting, they didn't show any consideration or follow-up. I can't leave my dog ​​there with peace of mind. I will never use their services again. I think other pet owners should be more careful.

They provide very thorough and detailed explanations before and after surgery.
The clinic is very clean.
All of the doctors are very trustworthy.

However, the location of the elevator can be a little difficult to find at first glance, and it can get a little hot inside the elevator in the summer.
